title: Restriction of scalars preserves limits
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], the functor $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$
preserves limits.

proof.text: Under the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] supplies the adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. Thus the restriction functor in the statement is the right adjoint of extension of scalars; this uses precisely the braided, coequalizer and tensor-colimit hypotheses already assumed, and no closedness or coextension of scalars.

Let $I$ be any small category, let $F:I\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$ be a diagram, and let $(L,(\pi_i)_i)$ be any limit cone of $F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] to the adjunction of step 1, with $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$, $\mathcal C$ there equal to $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ here, and $R=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. It says exactly that $(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L,(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\pi_i)_i)$ is a limit cone for $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ F$. Since the shape and the existing limit cone were arbitrary, restriction preserves limits (in every size for which the diagram and cone are defined). This is a preservation assertion and does not assert existence of all limits in either module category.
